newsitem.title: THAILAND: Vietnam seeks foreign partners in rubber industry.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks foreign partners in rubber industry.

text.p: Vietnam is seeking more joint ventures with foreign partners to develop its rubber industry, a senior Vietnamese official said on Monday.

Harrisons Malayalam Company of India, for example, was in the process of launching a joint venture with the state-run General Rubber Corporation of Vietnam (GERUCO), said GERUCO deputy director general Le Van Binh.
The project would involve 20,000 hectares of rubber plantations, he told the Asia International Rubber Conference. He did not disclose the value of the joint venture.
Boosting foreign investment in the industry was a part of the country's first ever master plan on rubber development, which will cover 1996-2005.
"In the investment in the rubber industry in Vietnam, GERUCO has policy of joint venture and cooperation with foreign and local partners to mobilise capital for rubber development," he said.
The move was also meant to improve technology transfer from foreign countries, he said.
Vietnam aimed to boost its natural rubber output at an annual rate of 15-20 percent in 1996-2005 from around 150,000 to 160,000 tonnes expected this year, Binh told the conference.
To facilitate investment, the National Assembly of Vietnam would be amending foreign investment laws.
